children.value: Confidence that watches accuracy, not just speed
The core signal for how well you know a key has always been how
you type it. KeyLearn now adds a second opinion drawn from learning science — a technique called

you hit that key. It forgives the occasional slip on a key you clearly know, and it refuses to be fooled by a lucky fast-but-sloppy tap. The two views are blended together, with raw speed still leading by two-to-one, so a letter only counts as mastered when you're both quick
accurate. It's tuned to unlock the next letter at the same comfortable pace you're used to — usually a couple of clean passes — just with a sharper eye on mistakes.
